note.text:
Some important types of chemical reaction:
• Combination (synthesis): two substances join to make one. Iron + sulphur → iron sulphide.
• Decomposition: one substance breaks into simpler ones, often by heating. Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide.
• Combustion (burning): a substance reacts with oxygen and gives out heat and light. Methane (gas) + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.
• Displacement: a more reactive element pushes a less reactive one out of its compound. Zinc + copper sulphate → zinc sulphate + copper.
• Neutralisation: an acid reacts with a base to give a salt and water. Sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → sodium chloride + water.
Everyday examples: cooking, digestion, respiration, photosynthesis, rusting, souring of food.

cards.idea: Combination: two substances join to make one product. Decomposition: one substance breaks into simpler substances.
example: Heating limestone gives lime and carbon dioxide (decomposition).

cards.idea: Combustion is burning in oxygen, giving out heat and light. Neutralisation is acid + base → salt + water.
example: Cooking gas burning on a stove.
Sodium hydroxide + hydrochloric acid → salt + water.

cards.idea: Displacement: a more reactive metal takes the place of a less reactive one in its compound.
example: Zinc + copper sulphate → zinc sulphate + copper.

pick.q: Zinc is more reactive than copper. What happens when zinc is put in copper sulphate solution?
pick.r: Copper is displaced and zinc sulphate forms.
e: Zinc is more reactive, so it does react.
The more reactive metal stays in the compound, not out of it.
No oxygen is made here.
pick.y: The more reactive metal takes the place of the less reactive one.

pick.q: Copper is less reactive than iron. Will copper displace iron from iron sulphate?
e: A less reactive metal cannot push out a more reactive one.
Temperature does not change the order of reactivity.
Light does not matter.
pick.y: Only a more reactive metal can displace another.

pick.q: What is given out when a substance burns?
e: Oxygen is used up when things burn.
Water may form, but heat and light are always given out.
Burning gives out heat and light.
pick.y: Combustion gives out heat and light.

pick.q: What does an acid react with in neutralisation?
e: Two acids do not neutralise each other.
That is combustion.
Noble gases do not react.

pick.q: Which everyday process is a chemical reaction?
e: Drying is evaporation: physical.
Melting is physical.
Grinding only makes small pieces.
pick.y: Digestion breaks food into new substances.
